editorial:
Imagine being part of a legendary army that suddenly loses everything. You get to see Guts return to his old friends just as things are falling apart, and the tension is high from the start. The bond between Guts and Casca is the heart of the story, making you really care about them while they deal with the fallout of Griffith's downfall. It feels like a dark fairy tale where the stakes keep getting higher, and you can feel the dread building up as the characters try to find some peace in a world that wants to tear them apart.

The action scenes are wild, though some of the computer graphics can look a bit stiff if you are used to modern anime. However, the emotional weight of the story makes up for it. The pacing starts slow but turns into a total nightmare in the best way possible. It is a perfect pick for anyone who likes stories about loyalty and betrayal.
endingExplained: Everything goes wrong when Griffith uses a magical item called the Behelit to save himself. He sacrifices all his loyal soldiers to demons to become a god-like being. You see the Band of the Hawk get slaughtered in a huge bloodbath. Guts and Casca barely survive, but they are scarred forever. Griffith is reborn as Femto, and Guts is left with a brand on his neck that attracts monsters every night.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark fantasy and epic tragedies.
